stances.claim: Incoming BIR Commissioner Lilia Guillermo answered TV journalists prudently -- needing 'correct data' before a definitive commitment on the Marcos estate-tax liability allegedly ballooned to over P203 billion from the original P23 billion -- and tellingly indicated she would ask BBM, 'P'wede ba maging role model kayo? (Can you be a role model?)'

The 'correct data' are already publicly knowable from the Supreme Court e-library and the relevant Court of Appeals decision -- and they establish that the assessments lapsed into finality after the Marcoses failed to administratively protest within the 30-day NIRC window, and that the deficiency tax assessments were properly served (San Juan 1991; BBM's House office 1992; estate lawyer Dean Antonio Coronel) with conferences offered 'to no avail.'

Marcos II v. CA (June 5, 1997) -- penned by Justice Justo P. Torres Jr. and concurred in unanimously by Justices Florenz D. Regalado (Division chair), Flerida Ruth P. Romero, Reynato S. Puno, and Vicente V. Mendoza -- dismissed BBM's appeal, holding that BIR assessments 'are presumed correct and made in good faith' and that 'the taxpayer has the duty of proving otherwise,' and characterizing BBM's course of action as reflecting 'his disregard or even repugnance of the established institutions for governance in the scheme of a well-ordered society.'

Notably, the petitioner was named 'Ferdinand R. Marcos II' -- not 'Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.' -- in the title and consistently in the textual content of the 1997 SC decision. This naming consistency is significant.

The proper next steps are factual-procedural questions for the BIR to answer: how much has been collected from the levy and auction sale? How much remains? How was the P23 billion originally computed? How did it balloon to P203 billion? What other Marcos-estate properties remain to satisfy both the original assessment and the balloon? What collection actions, if any, will BIR undertake? Is BIR open to a compromise?

notable_anecdotes: Commissioner Guillermo's viral June 23 reply -- 'P'wede ba maging role model kayo?' (Can you be a role model?) -- preserved as the column's seed and the most-shared single-line institutional question of the transition.

The June 27, 1990 BIR Special Tax Audit Team's mandate to investigate 'the late president, as well as that of his family, associates and cronies' -- preserved with the original 'cronies' framing intact.
The July 5, 1993 public auction with 'no bidder' -- lots forfeited in favor of the government -- preserved as the procedural detail that converted assessments into collected real properties.

The Marcos II v. CA holding's most quotable line: '[A]ssessments [of the BIR] are presumed correct and made in good faith. The taxpayer has the duty of proving otherwise... The course of action taken by petitioner reflects his disregard or even repugnance of the established institutions for governance in the scheme of a well-ordered society.' -- preserved as the column's doctrinal anchor and the most pointed line in the 25-year-old precedent.

The naming observation: the petitioner appears as 'Ferdinand R. Marcos II' (not 'Jr.') consistently in both the title and textual content -- a fact flagged as 'significant' without further elaboration, inviting reader inference.

one_paragraph_summary: When TV journalists pressed incoming BIR Commissioner Lilia Guillermo on how she would address the Marcos estate-tax liability -- allegedly ballooned to over P203 billion from the P23 billion originally assessed -- she 'answered prudently' that she needed to see 'correct data' before committing, and famously said she would ask President-elect BBM, 'P'wede ba maging role model kayo? (Can you be a role model?)' -- going viral on June 23. Panganiban argues the 'correct data' are already publicly knowable from the Supreme Court e-library and the relevant Court of Appeals decision. The undisputed factual record: Marcos died September 29, 1989 in Honolulu; on June 27, 1990, the BIR created a Special Tax Audit Team to investigate the Marcoses and 'family, associates and cronies'; the investigation found the Marcoses failed to file written notice of death, an estate tax return (ETR), and income tax returns (ITRs) for 1982-1986 -- 'all in violation of the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC).' On July 26, 1991, BIR issued deficiency assessments (over P23B estate tax; smaller ITR deficiencies for the spouses and BBM personally), served at the Marcoses' San Juan address (1991), BBM's House of Representatives office (1992), and via the late Dean Antonio Coronel as estate lawyer (Mrs. Marcos invited to a conference 'to no avail'). The assessments were never administratively protested within the 30-day NIRC window -- and thus lapsed into finality. In 1993, BIR issued notices of levy on Marcos real properties; on July 5, 1993, a public auction was held but 'there being no bidder, the lots were declared forfeited in favor of the government.' BBM sued in the CA on June 25, 1993, lost, and (as administrator of his father's estate, with Mrs. Marcos) elevated to the SC. In Marcos II v. Court of Appeals (June 5, 1997, Second Division, ponente Justo P. Torres Jr., concurred in unanimously by Justices Florenz D. Regalado, Flerida Ruth P. Romero, Reynato S. Puno, and Vicente V. Mendoza), the SC dismissed the appeal, holding that BIR assessments 'are presumed correct and made in good faith,' that 'the taxpayer has the duty of proving otherwise,' and characterizing BBM's course of action as reflecting 'his disregard or even repugnance of the established institutions for governance in the scheme of a well-ordered society.' Notably, the petitioner was named 'Ferdinand R. Marcos II' -- not 'Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.' -- in the title and textual content of the decision. CJ closes with a catalog of factual questions for the BIR: how much has been collected from the levy and auction? How much remains? How was the P23 billion computed? How did it balloon to P203 billion? What other estate properties remain? What collection actions will BIR undertake? Is BIR open to a compromise on the balloon or the original assessment? 'Let's await BIR's answers.'
